Jefferies lowered its 2026 revenue estimate by 1% and cut its 2026 and 2027 EPS...

items.title: Should You Buy Carnival Stock While Europe Sails Emptier?
items.summary: Carnival Corporation (CCL) trades near $22, down about 26% over the past year, while the S&P 500 gained close to 18%. The easy read on a cruise line that cheap is that demand finally cracked. It has not. Carnival lowered its 2026 yield outlook after the Middle East conflict hit its European sailings, and part of that cut was its own choice to protect price rather than fill cabins.

items.title: Iran “Offered” to Reopen the Strait of Hormuz. These Stocks Could Be the Biggest Winners
items.summary: A senior Iranian official told a Japanese news agency that Tehran could reopen one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints within seven days, and the stocks that stand to gain the most are not the ones the market moved on Friday.

items.title: Royal Caribbean Group Falls 5% on $3B Sandals Resorts Stake; Carnival and Norwegian Slide 3%
items.summary: Royal Caribbean just staked billions on a land resort brand, and the market is punishing the stock hard while dragging its cruise rivals down with it. Whether that selloff reflects a smart bet mispriced by panic or a genuine strategic misfire is the question every cruise investor faces this morning.

items.title: How Is Carnival Corporation Stock Performance Compared to Other Leisure and Entertainment Stocks
items.summary: Carnival Corporation has significantly lagged its peers over the past year, even as Wall Street analysts remain strongly optimistic about the company’s future prospects.

items.title: Royal Caribbean Buys 50% Stake in Sandals Resorts for $3 Billion
items.summary: Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd. agreed to buy a 50% stake in Sandals Resorts International for about $3 billion, a deal that will give the cruise operator access to its all-inclusive resorts across the Caribbean.
